preamble.summary: Leviticus is moderately attested at Qumran. The most striking witness is **11QpaleoLevᵃ** (11Q1), copied in paleo-Hebrew script — like 4QpaleoExodᵐ for Exodus, the choice of archaic script reflects priestly scribal circles. 11QpaleoLevᵃ preserves a text very close to MT, with primarily orthographic variation. Leviticus 11 (clean/unclean food laws, paralleling Deut 14) and Leviticus 16 (Day of Atonement) are partially preserved in multiple manuscripts.
preamble.notable_variants: No major content variants. The 11QpaleoLevᵃ readings are notable for their script (paleo-Hebrew) more than their text. The Leviticus DSS witnesses overwhelmingly support the MT consonantal text against the LXX (which has more interpretive expansion in the cultic legislation).
preamble.coverage_assessment: fragmentary; ~250 verses attested across the listed manuscripts.
